A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GenPercept study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V3 reports original experiments on depth, surface normals, segmentation and matting, plus component ablations and appendix results on human pose estimation.

after.justification: V4 retains these original results and adds runtime measurements, training-data-volume experiments, stronger benchmark comparisons and general-object matting results.

M1.justification: The deterministic one-step GenPercept procedure, U-Net fine-tuning, optional decoders and task-specific losses are retained. The clarified UperNet output format and applications to additional datasets do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Matting coverage expands substantially beyond portraits: v4 adds zero-shot AIM500 evaluation and Composition-1K training, including semi-transparent and hollow objects (Table 10; Appendix H.4; Figures 16–17). It also adds ADE20K training, whereas v3 used ADE20K only for zero-shot evaluation on overlapping semantic classes.

E2.justification: V4 adds MVANet to DIS comparisons, Mask2Former with ResNet50/Swin-T/Swin-L to semantic segmentation, and ViTAE-S to matting comparisons. Table 6 also adds DMP Official to the final depth comparison, although DMP already participated in v3's ablations. These additions substantially strengthen comparator coverage across tasks.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include 1024-pixel DIS inference, training subsets ranging from 90K to 5.6K images, and runtime/memory measurements averaging 100 images at 768×768 on an RTX 4090 (Tables 8, 11–12). Supervised ADE20K and matting-transfer evaluations also introduce additional settings. The newly identified Marigold/DSINE protocols for retained geometry scores are documentation, not evidence that those experiments changed.

E4.justification: V4 adds training-volume sensitivity, runtime/ensemble/decoder comparisons, and synthetic-versus-real training comparisons under challenging visual conditions (Tables 11–12; Figure 9). Expanded cross-dataset DIS comparisons and portrait-to-general-object matting tests provide additional robustness evidence. The original architecture, timestep, prompt and training-strategy ablations remain.

E5.justification: Section 3.1 newly reports varying random seeds during training and inference when investigating scheduler performance. V3 does not report these checks. V4 provides no run counts, seed identifiers, error bars or confidence intervals, so this is a limited reporting addition rather than a documented increase in repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include supervised ADE20K mIoU of 50.2, AIM500 SAD of 75.5 versus ViTAE-S's 112.52, 1024-pixel DIS results, runtime measurements and data-volume results (Tables 8–12, 14). Tables 6–7 add baseline entries distinguished from authors' evaluations. Retained GenPercept geometry and pose scores are unchanged; the added training and inference settings should not be read as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly gives an explicit mathematical definition of the variance schedule using interpolation between square-root endpoints (v4 Equation 5). The diffusion objectives and one-step reduction otherwise retain v3's mathematics; equations brought into the main text largely restate material already in v3 Appendix A.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace the explicit finding that stochasticity harms perception with the scheduler-special-case claim that multi-step generation can become one-step without performance loss. The principal contributions—GenPercept, data-quality analysis and task-specific supervision—remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 replaces the earlier Gaussian-versus-RGB difficulty explanation with ground-truth shortcuts and training/inference mismatch; new Appendix B develops this interpretation. V4 acknowledges weaker benchmark performance against MVANet and ViTAE-S while emphasizing generalization, recommends depth versus disparity by scene type, and identifies LAION data scale versus diffusion pretraining as an unresolved source of benefits.

D1.justification: V4 specifies scheduler interpolation and UperNet class-channel outputs, identifies geometry results evaluated using released weights and Marigold/DSINE protocols, and documents runtime hardware and measurement settings. Existing training hyperparameters largely persist. The GenPercept code URL in v3's abstract is removed without replacement, reducing documented access information.

R1.justification: V4 replaces the DINO object-detection citation with Caron et al.'s self-supervised vision-transformer work, adds DINOv2 discussion, and cites the newly included comparators and Composition-1K source. Most of the related-work narrative and the positioning around repurposing diffusion priors remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries and Section 3.1 undergo substantial rewriting, including an equation-led explanation and a different mechanism narrative. Findings and conclusions are revised, the appendix is reorganized into additional thematic sections before the references, and matting implementation details move into the appendix.

P2.justification: V4 expands comparison tables and adds provenance markers, training/test-dataset columns, and runtime/data-volume tables. Figures 5–6 gain comparator columns; the cross-dataset segmentation display expands considerably; new synthetic-versus-real and general-matting figures appear. Figure 2's plot styling and several captions change. Numerous older qualitative panels are retained despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially strengthens previously under-supported practical claims through measured runtime and data-volume analyses, stronger baselines, and broader generalization tests. Tables 8–10 also expose task-specific weaknesses and produce more balanced conclusions, while baseline-provenance disclosures improve interpretability. These gains outweigh removal of the code link and reporting weaknesses: seed variation remains unquantified, and Appendix C's claimed 27% GPU-memory reduction conflicts with Table 11's 6.95-to-6.32 GB change, approximately 9%.
